claims.text: Psychological well-being among US 8th, 10th, and 12th graders suddenly decreased after 2012.
Adolescents who spent more time on electronic communication and screens had lower psychological well-being.
Adolescents who spent less time on nonscreen activities had lower psychological well-being.
Adolescents spending a small amount of time on electronic communication were the happiest.
Psychological well-being was lower in years when adolescents spent more time on screens.
Psychological well-being was higher in years when adolescents spent more time on nonscreen activities.
Changes in activities generally preceded declines in psychological well-being.
Cyclical economic indicators such as unemployment were not significantly correlated with psychological well-being.
The decrease in adolescent psychological well-being may be at least partially due to the rapid adoption of smartphones and the subsequent shift in time use.

evidence.description: In nationally representative yearly surveys of US 8th, 10th, and 12th graders 1991-2016 (N = 1.1 million), psychological well-being (self-esteem, life satisfaction, happiness) suddenly decreased after 2012.
Adolescents spending more time on social media, the Internet, texting, and gaming had lower psychological well-being.
Adolescents spending less time on in-person social interaction, sports/exercise, homework, and attending religious services had lower psychological well-being.
Adolescents spending a small amount of time on electronic communication reported the highest happiness.
Psychological well-being was lower in years when adolescents spent more time on screens.
Psychological well-being was higher in years when adolescents spent more time on nonscreen activities.
Changes in daily activities generally preceded declines in adolescent psychological well-being.
Cyclical economic indicators such as unemployment were not significantly correlated with well-being.
Lack of correlation with economic indicators suggests the Great Recession was not the cause, pointing instead to smartphone adoption and shifts in time use.

methodologies.name: Nationally representative yearly survey analysis
methodologies.description: Analyzed long-term repeated cross-sectional survey data tracking psychological well-being and activity time use among US adolescents.
datasets: Nationally representative yearly surveys of US 8th, 10th, and 12th graders
